tree.text: the term “Federal law enforcement assistance” means funds, equipment, training, intelligence information, and personnel,
the term “Federal law enforcement community” means the heads of the following departments or agencies:

children.text: the Criminal Division of the Department of Justice,
the National Security Division of the Department of Justice,
the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives, Department of Justice, and
other Federal agencies with specific statutory authority to investigate violations of Federal criminal laws,

tree.text: the term “law enforcement emergency” means an uncommon situation which requires law enforcement, which is or threatens to become of serious or epidemic proportions, and with respect to which State and local resources are inadequate to protect the lives and property of citizens or to enforce the criminal law, except that such term does not include—

children.text: the perceived need for planning or other activities related to crowd control for general public safety projects, or
a situation requiring the enforcement of laws associated with scheduled public events, including political conventions and sports events, and

tree.text: the term “State” means any State of the United States, the District of Columbia, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, the Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, the Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands, or the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands.

notes.text: References in TextThis chapter, referred to in text, was in the original “this subdivision” probably meaning subtitle B (which probably should have been designated “subdivision” B) of division I of chapter VI of title II of Pub. L. 98–473, which enacted this chapter.
Codification Section was formerly classified to section 10502 of Title 42, The Public Health and Welfare, prior to editorial reclassification and renumbering as this section.
